name: variant-sweep-phenotype
title: Variant-sweep phenotype — config-declared perturbation sweeps as phenotype comparisons

glossary.definition: A perturbation written into a config's `variants` block (via the fork's variant grammar), expanded into a grid of parameter dictionaries and applied to sim_data one grid point at a time.
The `v2ecoli.composites.vecoli.vecoli` composite run in whole-config mode: it loads a full fork config natively and runs it as one process-bigraph node, faithful to the fork's own architecture.
A caller-declared set of bulk molecule ids emitted from the followed cell each tick, collected across the variant sweep to trace the phenotype response.
The ordered set of variant indices (e.g. increasing dose or perturbation strength) against which the observables are compared -- the x-axis of the phenotype response.

biological_story:
A whole-cell model answers "what changes when one thing changes?" A config variant is exactly that one change, expressed declaratively -- a timeline event, a knockout, a parameter shift -- and a variant grid enumerates a sweep of it. The interesting biology is rarely the endpoint of a single run; it is the shape of the response as the perturbation strengthens.

This pattern reads that shape directly. Each grid point is applied to sim_data, the model runs, and a chosen set of molecular observables is emitted from the followed cell. Laid side by side across the sweep, the observables trace how the cell's internal state moves with the perturbation -- an uptake curve, a free-to-bound shift of a target, a growth response. Because the sweep is driven entirely by the config's own variant grammar and the observables are just declared paths, the same machinery serves a genotype sweep, an environmental dose, or a parameter scan without new code.

The member demonstration study exercises the pattern on a neutral, built-in variant so the mechanism is visible without committing to any particular biology; real applications supply their own config and markers.
question: How does a config-declared variant sweep move a whole-cell phenotype, read across the sweep axis?

executive.what_is_this:
A generic pattern for turning a config's declared `variants` grid into a
phenotype comparison. The whole-config node (`v2ecoli.composites.vecoli.vecoli`)
loads any fork config natively, applies one grid point of its `variants` block
to `sim_data`, emits a caller-chosen set of bulk observables, and runs. Sweeping
the variant index and comparing the observables across the sweep axis gives a
dose-response-style readout for whatever the config perturbs.

Nothing here is specific to a model or a perturbation: the config, the swept
parameter, and the observed molecule ids are all inputs. This investigation is
the reusable home for that pattern; a downstream repo instantiates it by copying
the member study and naming its own config, variant, and observables.
